basis: Congenital neutropenia is an immunodeficiency; recurrent oral ulceration and periodontal injury occur in 30-79%. Separately diagnosed infections do not establish other organ involvement.
Autoimmune injury of intestinal mucosa defines this enteropathy.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability define the syndrome; strabismus and impaired vision occur in 30-79%. Constipation and nonspecific respiratory findings do not establish organ damage.
Glaucoma is an ocular disorder causing optic nerve damage.
Benign neoplasm arising in cutaneous sweat glands.
Glycogen metabolism disorder with predominant hepatic storage, hepatomegaly and frequent fibrosis. Muscle weakness occurs in 3/15, below 30%.
Fibrotic replacement of lung parenchyma defines the disease. Right heart failure is a separately diagnosed complication; immune causes do not define the umbrella.
Myopathy, metabolic acidosis and sensorineural deafness define the syndrome. Seizures, dystonia and spasticity support CNS involvement in 1/1 phenotyped patient; evidence is sparse.
Immune-mediated destructive hemispheric encephalitis causes seizures, cerebral atrophy and progressive neurological loss.
Bacterial infection umbrella; no particular damaged organ is consistently established across its clinical forms.
Hereditary corticospinal tract disease with spasticity, hyperreflexia and Babinski signs in 4/4 patients.
Autoimmune injury of the musculoskeletal system defines this umbrella; additional organs depend on the subtype.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with severe neurodegeneration; retinopathy/optic neuropathy and gastrointestinal dysmotility requiring tube feeding each occur in 80-99%.
Facial skeletal overgrowth and strabismus/amblyopia define the syndrome. Dental open-bite malocclusion occurs in 30-79%; cleft palate is below 30%.
Exophthalmic ophthalmoplegia denotes thyroid-associated immune orbitopathy with impaired ocular movement. Associated thyroid disease is separately diagnosed.
Structural defect of the vertebral pars interarticularis.
Persistent dyskinesia is a neurological movement disorder; medication causation does not change the affected primary organ.
Carcinoma originates in the gallbladder or extrahepatic bile ducts, both hepatic-axis structures. Adjacent organ invasion lacks a qualifying frequency.
Congenital aneurysmal structural disease of the great vessels.
Hypomyelinating neuropathy and congenital joint contractures define the syndrome. Vocal cord paralysis causes laryngeal functional loss in 1/1 assessed patient; evidence is sparse.
Absent penile urethra with abnormal urinary drainage supports renal involvement. Supplied HPO reports anorectal malformations and pulmonary hypoplasia in 80-99%; penis itself has no axis.
Inherited osteosclerosis from defective bone resorption. Marrow failure and cranial nerve complications do not affect most patients across dominant forms.
Luft disease: uncoupled oxidative phosphorylation in skeletal muscle causes hypermetabolism and mitochondrial myopathy.
Acute mixed-lineage leukemia of hematopoietic blasts. The lymphoma ancestor does not make this leukemia a lymphoma or immune-mediated disease.
Brain, eye and skeletal defects define COFS1. Sensorineural hearing loss occurs in 1/3 (~33%); dental disease and metabolic findings omitted by cap. Recurrent pneumonia is a separate infection.
